name: Rye-grass pollen extract
short: Bee pollen, a different product, caused anaphylaxis in two case reports (both people with seasonal allergic rhinitis). Rye-grass pollen extract trials in men: rare, mild adverse events.
text: In men with benign prostatic hyperplasia, a systematic review of the rye-grass pollen extract (444 men in 2 placebo-controlled and 2 comparative trials lasting 12 to 24 weeks) found adverse events rare and mild (withdrawal rates 4.8% with the extract and 2.7% with placebo), while noting the trials were short, small and used preparations of unknown quality; a review of all published clinical trials of flower pollen extract in chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome (the abstract does not name the plant source of the pollen; 6 uncontrolled studies with 206 patients and 4 randomized trials with 384 patients) reported no significant adverse events, and a 12-week placebo-controlled trial in 139 men with this condition (70 given a standardised pollen extract as oral capsules) described adverse events as minor in all patients (the trial abstract identifies its extract only by a product name, the same one the systematic review above uses for the rye-grass pollen extract). None of these abstracts reports allergic reactions or says whether people with pollen allergy were included. For a different product, bee pollen (pollen granules packed by honey bees) taken by mouth, two case reports describe anaphylaxis: in a 40-year-old man with seasonal allergic rhinitis one hour after one tablespoon (the bee pollen contained Japanese hop, chrysanthemum, ragweed and dandelion pollens, and he had specific IgE to ragweed, chrysanthemum and dandelion) and in a 26-year-old woman with seasonal allergic rhinitis who later developed allergic asthma; the authors of the first report cautioned about the risk of severe allergic reactions on swallowing bee pollen, especially in people with pollen allergy. The abstracts do not say whether this applies to rye-grass pollen extract. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
